research_question_verbatim: Across All_Beauty, Appliances, Electronics, and Beauty_and_Personal_Care, does adding the text of a product’s first five valid observed reviews to the ratings and timing of those same reviews improve out-of-sample prediction of the proportion of one- and two-star ratings among its next ten observed reviews? Does the combined approach also outperform a simple category-adjusted rating baseline, and how do prediction gains and human-review prioritization benefits differ across categories?
question_summary_fa: آیا افزودن متن پنج نقد معتبرِ مشاهده‌شدهٔ نخست هر محصول به اطلاعات ساختاری همان پنج نقد، سهم امتیازهای ۱ و ۲ در ده نقد معتبرِ مشاهده‌شدهٔ بعدی را خارج از نمونه بهتر پیش‌بینی می‌کند، و آیا تفاوت در چهار دسته وجود دارد؟

study_unit.observation_not_census: first observed valid does not imply first ever published

time.horizon: next ten observed valid nonduplicate reviews; not a fixed number of days
time.tie_boundary_policy: exclude product from primary cohort if t5=t6, or if review 16 exists and t15=t16

target.unknown_next_ten: missing outcome, never encoded as zero

primary_hypothesis.S: ratings and historical timing from reviews 1-5 plus category
primary_hypothesis.ST: same structural inputs plus titles/bodies of reviews 1-5
primary_hypothesis.controls: same products, split, model family and comparable tuning budget
primary_hypothesis.effect: paired squared-loss improvement averaged equally over four categories

secondary_comparators: B1 category-adjusted smoothed early low-star share

decision.action: rank eligible products for human review

phase1_boundary.purpose: describe distributions, relationships, populations, cohort and leakage risks

historical_leakage_blocklist: t15 and label maturity as predictors
split_status: design only; calendar boundaries pending; enforce global product and label maturity in future modeling
